title: Pro-etale coinduction of supported finite scalar models
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E\}$, with discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring on profinite sets is $P\mapsto C(P,\Lambda)$, using all continuous maps. On each scheme $V$, put $\Lambda_V=p_V^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_V=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_V}$, with ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories and actual module-derived global sections to abelian groups [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-sfb-condensed-module-sections]. Use the small sites and indexing universe of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention].
For each quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $V$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], a support chain is a finite chain $W=V_s\to\cdots\to V_0=V$, each arrow a quasi-compact open immersion or a closed immersion with quasi-compact open complement [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $J$ be the composite of ordinary $a_!$ on open arrows and ordinary $a_*$ on closed arrows, with the identity for the empty chain [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek, def-sfb-module-lower-star]. A finite scalar local model on $W$ is a module locally on a pro-étale cover isomorphic to $\Lambda_W\otimes_{\underline\Lambda}\underline P$ for a finitely presented scalar $\Lambda$-module $P$, where both underlines denote discrete constant sheaves and $P$ may vary with the cover member [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Let $\mathcal G_V$ be the intersection of all full replete classes in $D(\mathcal A_V)$ containing $JL[0]$ for all such chains and models $L$ and satisfying the following conditions. They contain zero and are closed under isomorphisms, all integer shifts, distinguished-triangle extensions, and retracts [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. A retract of $K$ is given by maps $K\xrightarrow{i}L\xrightarrow{p}K$ with $pi=1_K$. They are closed under all small products in the ordinary derived category [def-weil-category-product]. If $I$ is a small filtered category and $C_i^\bullet$ is a strict diagram of module-sheaf complexes with a common termwise lower bound, and all $Q(C_i^\bullet)$ belong to the class, then $Q(\varinjlim_i C_i^\bullet)$ belongs to the class. Here the colimit is termwise in module sheaves and $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $U,V$ be quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes and let $b:U\to V$ be an object of the small pro-étale site of $V$ (thus a weakly étale morphism), also quasi-compact and quasi-separated [sk-def-pe-morphisms, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. No surjectivity or weak contractibility is assumed. For every support chain $W\to\cdots\to U$, its ordinary supported extension functor $J$, and every finite scalar local model $L$ on $W$ as defined above, the actual ordinary module-derived direct image satisfies
$$ Rb_*\bigl((JL)[0]\bigr)\in\mathcal G_V. $$
Here $Rb_*$ is the total right derived functor of the actual coefficient-compatible module direct image, not a completed or solidified direct image. The conclusion concerns these explicit supported generators, rather than an arbitrary object satisfying local hull-membership. The empty chain, empty schemes, zero coefficients and zero models are included. No Noetherian, finite-type or cohomological-dimension hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Use the etale coinduction theorem for the fixed coefficient to obtain its quantified etale property on all qcqs schemes. Substituting it into conditional ind-etale continuity shows that every qcqs map locally admitting the specified finite affine ind-etale charts sends supported finite scalar generators into the target hull. This substitution does not assume descent of a local model to one etale stage.

proof.text: Choose the finite cover $q_a:D_a\to U$ supplied by the ind-etale Cech refinement theorem. Every iterated fibre product $D_{a_0\ldots a_n}$ is qcqs and its map to $V$ has exactly the finite affine ind-etale charts required in step 1. These are source covers, so no assertion of descent of hull-membership on $V$ is being used. Empty $U$ gives zero throughout and can be discarded.

proof.text: Put $N=JL$. Along any Cech projection $r:D_{a_0\ldots a_n}\to U$, base-change the entire support chain. The open and closed module base-change isomorphisms, iterated one edge at a time and transported through the exact internal/section-module equivalences, give $r^*JL\cong J' r_W^*L$. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness survive base change; the complementary open is the base change of the original complementary open. Restrict the cover trivializing $L$: on that cover the same constant presentation for the scalar module $P$ gives $\Lambda\otimes_{\underline\Lambda}\underline P$ after inverse image. Thus $r_W^*L$ is a finite scalar local model and $r^*N$ is a supported generator on the intersection. Step 1 now puts $R(b r)_*(r^*N[0])$ in $\mathcal G_V$.

proof.text: The finite covering family defines an epimorphism $D=\coprod_a h_{D_a}\to1$ in $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Apply the coherent Cech pushforward-model theorem with $f=b$ and the module $N$. It gives a nonnegative double complex $B^{n,q}$ on $V$, an isomorphism $Rb_*N[0]\cong Q\operatorname{Tot}B$, and column isomorphisms $QB^{n,\bullet}\cong R(bv_n)_*(N_n[0])$. Finite-family site geometry identifies $D^{n+1}$ with the finite disjoint union of the fibre products in step 2. Sections on a finite disjoint union are the product of the component sections, so its module direct image is the product of the component direct images; compatible finite products of injective resolutions compute their derived product. Slice localization identifies each component with its own pro-etale site, and exact module transport retains the pulled-back coefficient. Hence the column is a finite product of the objects in step 3 and belongs to $\mathcal G_V$. The augmentation is the actual derived restriction augmentation.

proof.text: Let $T_m$ be the total of columns $0,\ldots,m$, with the outgoing horizontal differential discarded. Projection $T_m\to T_{m-1}$ is a chain map whose kernel is $B^{m,\bullet}[-m]$ with the signed vertical differential. The degreewise short exact sequence gives a distinguished triangle. Starting at $T_0=B^{0,\bullet}$ and using step 4, shift and triangle-extension closure gives $QT_m\in\mathcal G_V$ for all $m\ge0$. These truncations are quotient complexes; no spurious inclusion as subcomplexes is used.

proof.text:
The projections $T_{m+1}\to T_m$ split on graded modules by insertion of a zero column. For $T=\operatorname{Tot}B$ there is a degreewise short exact sequence
$0\to T\to\prod_{m\ge0}T_m\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_{m\ge0}T_m\to0$,
where $(sx)_m$ is the projection of $x_{m+1}$. Indeed the kernel is the compatible sequences, and in degree $r$ the tower stabilizes once $m\ge r$, identifying its limit with $T^r$. For surjectivity, given $(y_m)$ set $x_0=0$ and recursively lift $x_m-y_m$ to $x_{m+1}$ using the graded splitting. This is a morphism of degree-$r$ sheaves, so it proves epimorphy without choosing objectwise preimages. Termwise products represent derived products. By step 5 both products lie in $\mathcal G_V$, and the short-exact-sequence triangle, rotation and shift closure put $QT$ there. The augmented-total isomorphism from step 4 proves the asserted membership of $Rb_*JL[0]$. All constructions retain zero models, zero rings and identity support chains.
